panel.summary: No end-to-end test exercises the webhook over real HTTP, so the guard's dependency on the main.ts raw-body hook is unverified
panel.evidence: yorkie-signature.guard.spec.ts fabricates the ExecutionContext and injects `rawBody` by hand (lines 21-31), and yorkie-event.controller.spec.ts calls `handleEvent` directly with the guard bypassed. Nothing asserts that a real `POST /internal/yorkie/events` (a) receives a populated `req.rawBody` from the bodyParser `verify` hook and (b) rejects an unsigned/wrongly-signed request through the actual guard/route pipeline. `packages/backend/test/*.e2e-spec.ts` contains no reference to the route, the controller, or the `x-signature-256` header. The security of this endpoint rests entirely on the main.ts↔controller path agreement (main.ts:27 vs yorkie-event.controller.ts:31,37), which no lane checks.
panel.finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-signature.guard.spec.ts::no end-to-end test exercises the webhook over real http, so the guard's dependency on the main.ts raw-body hook is unverified

coderabbit.summary: Use a past date in the `issuedAt` test to avoid time-dependent failures.
coderabbit.detail: **Use a past date in the `issuedAt` test to avoid time-dependent failures.** The test expects `touchUpdatedAt` to be called with `new Date('2026-07-10T06:03:13.331Z')`, but the controller clamps `issuedAt` to `now()` via `Math.min(issuedMs, now)`. If the test executes before that exact UTC moment, the clamp kicks in and `touchUpdatedAt` receives `now()` instead — causing a flaky failure. Using a clearly historical date eliminates this fragility.
coderabbit.finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-event.controller.spec.ts::use a past date in the `issuedat` test to avoid time-dependent failures.
